analyticalMisses.detail: COL, MIN, LAD, and KC F5-NO legs worked, but BAL and STL F5-NO losses show the contract-structure edge (tie protection) is separate from whether the underlying baseball handicap was actually correct. Continue evaluating (1) whether the baseball edge exists and (2) whether F5 NO is the best expression of it, separately.
analyticalMisses.title: Tie protection cannot rescue an incorrect baseball-side handicap

analyticalMisses.detail: Misiorowski pitched well (6.0 IP, 1 R) but recorded only 6 K against a 9+ threshold -- strong pitcher performance did not imply a cash on a high ladder rung. For 8+/9+/10+ thresholds, require a larger documented pricing error and/or reduce stake given substantial tail variance. Schlittler's 7+ cleared exactly at 7, a reasonable ladder rung by comparison.
analyticalMisses.title: Extreme strikeout thresholds need greater edge or smaller stake

analyticalMisses.detail: NYY-TOR and BAL-TB F5 unders won; MIA-CIN and CWS-DET lost. Do not conclude F5 unders are bad from this sample, but this was the worst-ROI family on 2026-08-15 besides the one-off team total. Require stronger pitcher/offense agreement rather than leaning on recent-form narratives alone.

analyticalWins.detail: Buying the opponent's F5-winner NO (so the preferred team's lead OR a tie both win) went 4-2 for +$15.40 and better matched starter-driven theses than three-way favorite F5 YES contracts. Prospective process finding only -- do not infer permanent profitability from six bets; needs a larger sample.

processErrors.detail: STL F5-NO and STL team-total-under were superficially different market families but shared one core thesis (Boyd/Chicago suppresses STL scoring); both lost together when STL scored 8. Future exposure controls should group wagers by underlying handicap driver.

processErrors.detail: MIA-CIN F5 under moved dramatically toward plus-money before execution. Reducing stake in response was good risk control, but a large adverse move like this should trigger a full re-handicap and more often turn a marginal bet into a PASS, rather than being read as simply a better price.
processErrors.title: Adverse market movement interpreted as a better price rather than a re-handicap trigger

processErrors.detail: MacKenzie Gore 7+ K at $25 was aggressive relative to the confidence/variance profile, especially on a slate that already carried substantial correlated pitcher exposure (four total pitcher-prop legs).
processErrors.title: Staking on a marginal, high-variance pitcher ladder

proposedInvestigations: Continue tracking the protected-F5-NO tie-protection strategy across a larger sample before treating it as a durable edge.
Separately evaluate, for BAL and STL specifically, whether the baseball-side handicap was wrong or whether F5 NO was simply the wrong expression of a real edge.

Build an explicit correlation-group tag keyed to underlying handicap driver (not market family) so same-thesis exposure like STL F5-NO + STL team-total-under is sized as one correlated position, not two independent ones.

Define a stake-scaling rule for pitcher strikeout/outs ladders: require materially larger documented pricing error and/or smaller stake at 8+/9+/10+ thresholds given tail variance shown by the Misiorowski result.
Define a re-handicap trigger for large pregame adverse price moves (like MIA-CIN) instead of treating the move itself as an improved price.

Continue archiving/calibrating hitter projections (no real-money hitter bets were placed from the unproven projection engine on 2026-08-15); do not promote them into production-confidence recommendations until the calibration sample supports it.
